alternate_names: Elder Mother Temple of Dewas Tekri
deities: Goddess Tulja Bhavani (as Badi Mata, the elder mother)
festivals: Ashvin (Shardiya) Navratri — lakhs of pilgrims visit Tekri

history.dynasty: Revered by the Holkar dynasty (of which Tulja Bhavani is the Kuldevi) and the Puar rulers of Dewas Senior/Junior states; legend links King Bharthari to a tunnel from the Tekri to Ujjain
history.period: Believed ancient ('anaadi kaal') with the present shrine dating back centuries; exact construction date undocumented
history.summary: The Tulja Bhavani shrine on Dewas Tekri — a ~300-ft hill above the city — is the 'Badi Mata' (elder mother) temple of the two sister goddesses of the hill. Local belief holds that Tulja Bhavani (elder sister) and Chamunda (younger sister) once resided together here but, after a dispute, began to leave; Lord Hanuman and Bhairav Baba intervened, so Tulja Bhavani remained half-sunk into the hill facing south while Chamunda stopped mid-descent facing north. Pilgrims doing the Tekri parikrama therefore begin with Tulja Bhavani's darshan and conclude with Chamunda. The idol is regarded as self-manifested (swayambhu) in an awakened state, and wishes made with a true heart are believed to be fulfilled. Tulja Bhavani is the Kuldevi (clan goddess) of the Holkar dynasty, while the younger Chamunda is the Kuldevi of the Puar dynasty — Dewas being noted as a city ruled by two dynasties. Dewas Tekri is also described as a Rakt Peeth (a spot where drops of Mata Sati's blood fell).

name: Jay Maa Tulja Bhavani (Badi Mata) Mandir
town_description: Dewas is a historic industrial city in western Madhya Pradesh, about 35 km northeast of Indore on the Malwa plateau. Its identity is dominated by the Tekri, a 300-ft hill in the middle of the city crowned by the two sister-goddess temples, and it was the seat of two princely states (Dewas Senior and Junior) under the Puars and Marathas. Devotees also pass through Dewas on Indore–Ujjain–Omkareshwar pilgrimage circuits.
